podcast.body: This album became instrumental in defining the chill-out genre, offering a relaxing and evocative sonic experience. It was designed to simulate a nocturnal journey along the southern coast of the United States, utilizing layers of ambient sounds, samples, and music that unfolded like a narrative. The recording was notable for being captured live in a single take, and its cover art drew direct inspiration from Pink Floyd's *Atom Heart Mother*. While Bill Drummond stated it was intended as a parody of progressive rock, which they found pretentious, the album paradoxically achieved cult classic status within electronic music. "El disco describó una experiencia sonora relajante y evocadora, diseñada para simular un viaje nocturno por la costa sur de Estados Unidos, con capas de sonidos ambientales, sampler y música que fluye como una narrativa."
